text_sources.what: Katana, Horikawa Kunihiro, c. Keicho 8 (1603). nagasa 70.2, sori 1.6, motohaba 3.05, sakihaba 2.5, kasane 0.75 / 0.55 cm; shinogi-zukuri, mitsu-mune, wide shinogi-ji, shinogi somewhat high, slight funbari, extended chu-kissaki; hamon low, shallow notare + ko-gunome; boshi sugu komaru, very shallow kaeri. Tensho-style koshirae: tsuka 24.5 cm leather-wrapped over red same, round iron tsuba 8.0 cm, shakudo nanako fuchi, crawling-dragon menuki
Hizen Tadayoshi I, 1615: 75.15 / 1.5 / 3.11 / 2.36 / 0.64 cm, 2 mekugi, gold single-foiled habaki
Kunihiro katana dated Keicho 15 (69.7 cm) and Keicho 16 (68.1 cm)
Takahiro, dated 1622: cutting edge 71.5 cm, curvature 1.5 cm
Munetsugu, early-mid 17th c.: cutting edge 80.8 cm, curvature 1.4 cm
Tadahiro II, dated 1632: cutting edge 66.9 cm, curvature 1.8 cm
TNM F-19992: red-lacquer uchigatana koshirae, Azuchi-Momoyama to Edo (16th-17th c.); blade 68.5 / 2.1 cm; mounting overall 93.0 cm; round iron openwork tsuba (two oxen)
Keicho-shinto sugata: long, wide, shallow sori, little taper, o- or extended chu-kissaki, low niku, thicker kasane; mitsu-mune among Soshu-den smiths
Juyo Tensho-era uchigatana koshirae: tsuka 26.1 cm, tsuka curvature 0.2 cm, lacquered black leather wrap, black lacquered horn kashira, round hammered iron tsuba, kaku-mimi ko-niku, no hitsu-ana
Tensho koshirae: black lacquered same, low-profile angled fuchi, leather wrap, black lacquered horn kashira with the wrap over it; tsuba typically iron; same lacquered before Momoyama, plain after
menuki: omote at or after the 3rd diamond from the fuchi, ura 3 diamonds from the kashira; the omote is the side seen when worn
nagasa = straight line from the munemachi to the tip; sori = deepest gap between that line and the mune; kasane at the munemachi / at the kissaki
kasane = the thickness of the mune
